about.title: Farmersville Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Farmersville's economy leans heavily on agriculture, packing, transport, and small local businesses along corridors like Farmersville Boulevard and W Visalia Road, and workplace injuries here often involve machinery, vehicles, or falls on job sites that aren't always straightforward. In California, workers' compensation is generally the exclusive path against your employer no matter who was at fault, but that's not the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim against that third party. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a cut of any settlement; we simply connect injured workers in Farmersville with an independent attorney who can look at both the workers' comp side and any third-party angle. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers something for you, and reaching out costs nothing. You focus on healing; let someone experienced sort out the claims.

items.title: We Look Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the only remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can open a separate injury claim. An independent attorney can help identify whether that applies to your situation.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing workers for reporting an on-the-job injury. If you've faced pushback after reporting within the required 30-day window, an attorney can advise you on your rights.

items.title: Deadlines Matter
items.desc: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline, separate from workers' comp reporting rules. Acting sooner preserves evidence and options before time runs out.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site off North Farmersville Boulevard. Can I still file a claim if it's been a few weeks?
items.answer: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer for workers' comp purposes, so acting quickly matters. If a third party was involved, that claim carries a separate two-year deadline. An independent attorney can review your timeline and explain what's still available to you.

items.question: My employer says workers' comp is my only option. Is that true?
items.answer: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of fault. However, if a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer contributed to your injury, you may be able to bring a separate third-party claim alongside your workers' comp case.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting an injury in Farmersville?
items.answer: No. California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against a worker for reporting a workplace injury. If you believe you've faced retaliation, it's worth speaking with an independent attorney about your options.
